chapter: Trumpeters he admired and the Ellington near-miss
title: Ellington finds something for every player
summary: Duke would listen to a player and then write something just right for him, as he would have for Red Allen, and the New Orleans sound was in his band.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, I established him, I think, Jonah. You know, before I think he was fighting for himself. Don't you?

Could have been, yeah. He could have been. I never really knew what it was, because it looked like he was getting -- one thing Duke would do, he wouldn't let you sit in there and not play. He would find something for you to do after he'd listened to you. He'd sit there and listen to you, and after he'd listened to you, he'd come out with something for you to play.
Yeah, right, just right for you.
Yeah, sure. I think he would have did that for Red Allen.
I think Duke would have did it for just about anybody.
Yeah, but see, he had that jungle in him, you know, that suited Duke very much.
He had a lot of Louis in him too, didn't
Sure. Sure. You could hear that New Orleans sound there.
